title: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies - National Values Education - Readiness in Marriage
exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which condition for marriage ensures that the couple has attained the appropriate biological age and bodily maturity for childbearing and domestic roles?
questions.explain: **Physical fitness** (and maturity) implies that the individuals' bodies are fully grown and physically capable of handling the physical demands of marriage, including childbearing.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When intending couples demonstrate the ability to handle stress, manage conflicts without violence, and show emotional maturity, they possess:
questions.explain: Mental stability, emotional maturity, and the capacity to deal with the inevitable pressures of marriage are categorized under **psychological fitness**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: A man and a woman wishing to marry must have a reliable source of income to cater to their future family's needs. This condition is termed:
questions.explain: The ability to independently pay for housing, food, and future child-rearing expenses constitutes **financial readiness**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: What is a very common consequence of entering into a marriage without psychological or financial readiness?
options: Automatic elimination of extended family interference
questions.explain: A lack of readiness often triggers stress, unmet expectations, and inability to manage disagreements, leading to **constant fighting and instability**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: When chronic marital instability and conflict escalate due to a severe lack of readiness, it frequently culminates in:
questions.explain: The ultimate consequence of prolonged instability, domestic conflict, and lack of readiness in a marriage relationship is the legal dissolution of the union, known as **divorce, resulting in broken homes**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Before getting married, intending couples are expected to possess 'social stability'. This condition implies that they should:
options: Have thousands of followers on social media platforms
Be highly involved in every communal conflict in their area
Possess a mature standing in society with good interpersonal relationships and respect for norms
Isolate themselves entirely from their extended family and friends
questions.explain: **Social stability** means the individuals have developed good interpersonal relationships, maturity, and are well-integrated and respected within their community's social norms.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: What is the primary effect of a 'broken home' on children, often resulting from a lack of marriage readiness?
options: They automatically receive free government scholarships
They suffer emotional trauma, lack of proper parenting, and possible exposure to crime
They experience sudden physical growth spurts and high immunity
They are immediately given political leadership roles in the community
questions.explain: A major effect of broken homes (caused by divorce or severe instability) is that children face emotional trauma, inadequate supervision, and are more vulnerable to juvenile delinquency.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: If an underaged child is forced into early marriage, which specific condition of readiness is most flagrantly violated?
questions.explain: An underaged child lacks both **physical fitness** (bodily maturity for childbearing) and **psychological fitness** (mental maturity for domestic and marital stress).
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios best demonstrates a lack of **financial readiness** in marriage?
options: A couple who saved money for three years before getting married
A man with no job, no savings, and no means of income deciding to take a wife
A woman who owns a thriving small-scale business and marries a teacher
A couple that plans a small, affordable wedding instead of a lavish one
questions.explain: **Financial readiness** requires a sustainable source of income to cater to a family's basic needs. Having no job or income explicitly shows a lack of this readiness.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education

questions.q: Consider the equation of marital success outlined by social counselors: $$ \text{Success} = f(\text{Physical}, \text{Psychological}, \text{Social}, \text{Financial Readiness}) $$. If financial and psychological readiness are missing, what is the most scientifically predictable outcome based on social studies principles?
options: High probability of divorce and domestic violence
questions.explain: When fundamental readiness conditions like psychological maturity and financial stability are zero or negative, the relationship naturally trends toward severe instability, constant fighting, and eventual **divorce**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
